AuditEntry.description:
One admin audit record. `outcome` is a stable token tooling can branch on. The record is
HASH-CHAINED for tamper-EVIDENCE: `hash` is the SHA-256 of bytes fixed by this record's own
`scheme` (the recipe is on `hash`), and `prev_hash` is the preceding entry's `hash`. Recomputing
the chain detects any altered/reordered/deleted entry (detection, not prevention; a compromised
host can still rewrite the whole chain; prevention is shipping the log off-box to a SIEM).

at_ms.description: Epoch milliseconds of the same instant as `ts`, sealed by scheme 4; absent on older schemes.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

client_request_id.description:
Scheme 4: the caller's own `X-Request-Id`, kept beside the minted `request_id`; absent when
the request sent none (or an invalid one), and on older schemes.

config_generation.description:
The config generation after the change, as a decimal string: on every applied row of a
config-changing request, null otherwise.

data.description: Members typed per action. Always an object; `{}` when the action has none.

hash.description:
The tamper-evidence digest: lowercase hex SHA-256 over the bytes this record's `scheme` names.
Integers are written in decimal ASCII and strings as their UTF-8 bytes unless stated.

Scheme 1: `prev_hash|seq|ts|action|resource|outcome|principal`, the fields joined by `|`
(1.5.5's formula).

Scheme 2: `prev_hash|seq` as in scheme 1, then one zero byte (0x00), then `ts`, `action`,
`resource`, `outcome` and `principal`, each as its byte length (8 bytes, big-endian) followed
by its bytes; `ts` is its 8-byte big-endian value, so its length is 8.

Scheme 3 (ADMIN-API-1.6 section 7.2): `prev_hash|seq` as before, then the row suffix: one 0x03
byte, `ts` as scheme 2 writes it, `action`, `resource`, `outcome` and `principal` each
length-prefixed, then `config_generation`, `request_id`, `idempotency_key`, `kind` and
`instance` (each length-prefixed: a single 0x00 byte when absent, 0x01 and the bytes when
present), `sections_changed` (an 8-byte big-endian count, then each name length-prefixed),
`severity` and `message` (length-prefixed) and `data` as one length-prefixed field holding its
canonical JSON (members in ascending order of their names' UTF-8 bytes, no whitespace,
minimal string escapes), so every member of `data` is inside the digest.

Scheme 4 (ADMIN-API-1.6-ONE-MODEL section 7.1): `prev_hash|seq` as before, then one 0x04 byte
and scheme 3's row fields in scheme 3's order and framing (`ts` is `at_ms` divided by 1000),
then `at_ms` as its 8-byte big-endian value, then `client_request_id`, `trace_id`,
`operation_id` and `on_behalf_of` (each framed like `request_id`), then `unconditional` as one
byte (0x01 when true, 0x00 when false), then `before_digest` and `after_digest` (framed like
`request_id`). A member this record does not serve is absent (a single 0x00 field).

idempotency_key.description: The request's `Idempotency-Key`, null when it carried none.

instance.description: The instance an engine event is about.

kind.description: The engine kind of the instance an engine event is about.

message.description: Core-written text for the row; empty for rows from before scheme 3.

operation_id.description:
Scheme 4: the operation the request created (`GET /operations/{key}` serves the same id);
absent when it created none, and on older schemes.

outcome.description:
Stable outcome token: `applied` (mutation committed) | `rejected` (validation/conflict, nothing
changed).

prev_hash.description:
The preceding entry's `hash` (empty for the first entry of the process, or the oldest retained
entry whose predecessor was pruned).

principal.description:
WHO: the authenticated principal id that attempted the mutation (`admin` for the operator
token; a virtual-key id or an external module's principal id otherwise). Attribution, never a
credential.

request_id.description: The admin request's id (its `X-Request-Id`), null for a row no request caused.

resource.description: The resource acted on (e.g. `hook:compress`). Never a secret.

scheme.description:
WHICH RECIPE `hash` was sealed under: 1 (the 1.5.5 pipe join), 2 (length-prefixed fields), 3 (the row fields)
or 4 (the row fields and the request fields); all are stated on `hash`. A record is sealed under 4
when it is written through the row path (`AUDIT.record_by` and `emit_row_now`: every admin
request's rows; an earlier engine sealed those under 3), under 1 otherwise when its
`action`, `resource` and `outcome` carry no `|`, and under 2 when they do, so its fields always
read back exactly. A
record without this field is scheme 1. A verifier checks each record under its own scheme.

sections_changed.description: The config sections the change touched (empty when it touched none, or none is known).

seq.description: Monotonic sequence number (1-based). It continues across restart: the chain is one durable log.

ConfigSettingsView.description:
`GET`/`PUT /config/settings` (1.5.0 full-config coverage): the API-settable single-value config
overlay (`root` section) and, on a PUT, the apply metadata. `settings` is the CURRENT effective
root override (the merge of prior overlay + this request). It is overlay-persisted so it survives
a restart. 1.5.3: a MUTABLE config always has a writable `config.overlay` backend (the boot
invariant), so a successful PUT is ALWAYS durable; a LOCKED config (`config.locked: true`) refuses
the PUT (`400`) instead of applying it in memory only; the silent-loss outcome is gone.
`reload_to_apply` names the fields whose new value is DURABLY STORED but not yet LIVE: the
process-level binds (`listen`/`admin_listen` socket, `tls`/`admin_tls` bind, and the
`admin_require_mtls` boot-guard) are read once at process start, and the durable `store` backend
is reused across a hot reload; none can hot-swap, so they take effect on the next RESTART (or a
supervisor restart), NEVER on a
`POST /config/reload`: a reload re-reads disk and rebuilds the `App` but does not rebind sockets,
rebuild the TLS acceptor, or re-open the store. It is always EMPTY when nothing was durably stored
(no overlay); `note` names the affected fields instead. Everything else
(`rate_card`/`per_request_fee`/`security`/`health`/`routing`) is LIVE on the swap;
`limits` is live EXCEPT four boot-scoped fields (see `reload_to_apply_fields`):
`upstream_request_timeout_secs`/`pool_max_idle_per_host`/`pool_idle_timeout_secs`, which the
reused `UpstreamClients` only reads once at boot, and `max_inbound_concurrent`, which is baked
once into the data router's `GlobalConcurrencyLimitLayer` at process start (a config apply swaps
only `Arc<App>`, never the router): two independent freezing mechanisms.
There is NO
`observability` section here, and no `metrics` one either: 1.5.3 DELETED both from the config
grammar, and `RootSettings` (what this endpoint projects) carries neither field: a PUT naming
`observability` is a loud `400` (`deny_unknown_fields`), never a silent no-op. All telemetry
egress uses the named `export:` map. Export definitions and explicit supported field projections
are authored through the named exporter routes or source-fenced configuration document edits.
Module-carried streams, produced fields and required pinned fields are published in the export
form schema; lifecycle and restart requirements remain explicit in mutation responses.
The settings endpoint exposes only the patchable advanced fields. The document-only
`advanced.shutdown.deregister_delay` is captured at boot and requires restart.
Within these settings, `advanced` is live EXCEPT `response_headers`: `response_headers.server_timing` is
baked into router middleware state at boot (same "config apply swaps `Arc<App>`, never the
router" freezing as `max_inbound_concurrent`) and is not rebuilt by an apply.

Fields that were stored durably but are RESTART-TO-APPLY: a socket rebind, a TLS acceptor
build and a store open all happen once at process start, so a `POST /config/reload` does NOT
make them live; `POST /restart` (or a supervisor restart) does. Empty when the PUT touched
only live-swappable fields (or on a GET). The field NAME is frozen wire; only this description
changed.

settings.description:
The current effective root-section overlay (only the fields the operator has set; base
`config.yaml` stands for the rest). An arbitrary JSON object (the `RootSettings` projection),
PROJECTED by `service::redact_settings_bags` through the secret rule (`v1/secret_rule.rs`): every
secret position (a secret-named field, an undeclared key of a `settings:` bag) is
`{set, secret_ref}`, never a value or a hash. Same on the GET and on the PUT echo.

This field NAME is frozen wire and is the response ENVELOPE member, not a plugin settings
bag; the redaction applies to the bags nested INSIDE it.

secret_ref.description: The reference text (`env:VAR`, `file:/path`, a secret module) when configured as one; null for an inline value

ConfigValidateView.description:
The result of `POST /api/v1/admin/config/validate`, a DRY-RUN: does a proposed config resolve +
validate, WITHOUT applying anything. `ok` is the verdict; `errors` lists every structural/resolution
failure at once (empty when `ok`). A well-formed request always returns 200 with this view (a valid
request that describes an INVALID config is `ok: false`, not an HTTP error); only a MALFORMED request
body is an `invalid_request`. Env-var interpolation is out of scope; this checks structure and
cross-reference resolution, not runtime secret presence.

snapshot rollback restores. Never contains a secret (hook definitions are operator config:
transports, grants, deadlines).

principal.description: The acting principal (audit attribution, same handle as the audit log).

summary.description: Human summary of the mutation that produced this version (e.g. `hook.register hook:x`).

ts.description: Unix seconds when the mutation committed.

CreateKeyReq.description:
`POST /keys` body (1.5.0 signed-token keys): PURE AUTH + a signed expiring token. A minted
key is a busbar-signed `{sub, exp, kid}` token, returned ONCE. No rpm/tpm/budget on a key - all
enforcement flows through the bound `group`. `#[serde(deny_unknown_fields)]` so the removed
1.4.x fields (max_budget_cents/rpm_limit/tpm_limit/budget_period) fail loudly.

admin.description:
Make this key an ADMIN credential (ADMIN-API r5 section 2.1): a scope ceiling and the verbs
held. Only a `full` principal may mint one, and an admin key carries no other grant.

allowed_pools.description: Pools this key may target. OMITTED = ALL pools; an explicit `[]` = NO pools.

audience.description: Optional exact resource audience for this bearer; omitted preserves ordinary key tokens.

expires_at.description: Token expiry as an absolute Unix-seconds timestamp. Mutually exclusive with `expires_in`.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

expires_in.description:
Token lifetime as a duration string (`7d`, `24h`, `30m`, `3600s`) - the token's `exp` is
`now + expires_in`. Mutually exclusive with `expires_at`. Absent (and no `expires_at`) => a
sane long default (see `DEFAULT_KEY_TTL_SECS`).

group.description:
The `groups:` bucket this key binds to (at most one). A key with NO group is authed +
unlimited (access only). If the named group EXISTS, the key binds to it. If it does NOT
exist, the mint 400s UNLESS `parent` is given, in which case it is AUTO-PROVISIONED as a leaf under
`parent` (self-service; see `parent`).

issue_aws_credential.description:
When true, ALSO issue an AWS-style access-key-id + secret access key (the MinIO/S3-compatible
model) so a Bedrock-SDK client can authenticate via inbound SigV4. Both are returned ONCE.

labels.description:
Optional mint-time labels echoed onto this key's metric series; never interpreted by
enforcement.

parent.description:
AUTO-PROVISION target: the EXISTING parent group under which to create
`group` as a leaf when `group` does not yet exist: the first-self-mint materialization of a
`user:<sub>` personal budget bucket. The new leaf's limits come from the nearest-ancestor
`child_default` template (inherit-only when none up the chain), created through the same
validate-at-the-door path as `POST /groups`. If `group` ALREADY exists, `parent` must equal
its actual parent (else 409); a mint never re-homes an existing group. Ignored when `group`
is absent (a key with no group has nothing to provision).

CreatedKeyView.description:
`POST /keys` (mint): the key metadata plus the ONCE-shown signed token, and (when an AWS SigV4
credential was requested) the AccessKeyId + secret access key. The AWS fields are absent on a
bearer-only mint.

admin.description: The admin grant (ADMIN-API r5 section 2.1): `{scope, verbs, verbs_all}`; `null` on a data-plane key.

aws_access_key_id.description: AWS AccessKeyId (present only when `issue_aws_credential` was set). Not secret.

aws_secret_access_key.description: AWS SigV4 secret access key, shown once (present only with an AWS credential).

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

credentials.description: The request-signing credential index: public ids only, never a secret.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

etag.description:
The key's ETag over its stored row (`If-Match` takes it). It never moves for a last-used
flush or a denylist sync; a rename, a rotation or any other edit of the row moves it.

expires_at.description: Unix-seconds expiry of the signed token.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

group_provisioned.description:
Whether this mint AUTO-PROVISIONED its bound group leaf (self-service); lets a portal
distinguish "bound to an existing bucket" from "created your personal bucket + bound".

minted_by.description: The principal that minted the key (an app-admin's id); `null` for a self-minted key.

minted_via.description: The identity-provider instance that minted a self-serve key.

origin.description: `"created"`, or `{"migrated_from": "1.5.5"}` for a key the migration carried over.

revocation.description: Why and when the key was revoked; `null` unless `state` is `revoked`.

state.description:
Same field as `KeyView.state`; a fresh mint is always `"active"` (enabled, not
revoked, not deleted).

token.description:
The busbar-SIGNED token: the key credential (1.5.0), shown EXACTLY once and never
returned by any read. (This is the field a client must capture to authenticate.)

config.description: The instance's configuration under the secret rule: a secret position is {set, secret_ref}

management.description: Availability describes a source mapping, not permission or guaranteed writability. Lifecycle schema is not the complete raw authoring grammar; source/precedence is revalidated at commit.

runtime.description: Closed and core-written for a plugin instance: settings, watchdog, crossings, dispatch, open, records, scrub, plane (each null where it does not apply); null for a core instance

state.description: The instance's own state answer; null before it has one

EffectiveConfigView.description:
The EFFECTIVE config snapshot (`GET /api/v1/admin/config`): the running configuration as busbar
resolved it, for drift detection (compare against your desired config) and one-shot inspection.
Composed from the same REDACTED reads as the individual endpoints (auth chain names, pool/model/
provider topology, hook definitions, global-hook wiring), so it carries NO secret: no client
tokens, no provider keys, no hook payloads. Additive-only; the source-layer annotation (base vs
overlay) lands with the config overlay substrate.

config_generation.description: The durable config generation at the time of this read (see `InfoView.config_generation`).

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

global_hooks.description:
Names fired on EVERY request: the hooks attached at the reserved all-pools key `pools.hooks:`
in `config.yaml` (the 1.5.3 replacement for the DELETED `global_hooks:` key; that key no
longer parses), plus any hook this API declares with `global: true`. The response FIELD name
stays `global_hooks`; only the config-file spelling changed.

reload_to_apply.description:
The plane sections the running configuration writes whose plane the process did not open at
boot: a plane is opened once, at process start, when its section is configured, so each is
stored and validated but serves nothing until the next RESTART. Omitted when none.

version.description:
The monotonic config version at the time of this read (see `InfoView.config_version`), so a
drift-detection read gets the config AND its version in one call.

code.description: The catalog code of this refusal; its page is https://getbusbar.com/docs/<major.minor>/errors/<code>.
Known server codes; forward-compatible readers preserve unknown code strings instead of failing the whole response.

details.description: Typed per reason (`x-busbar-reasons.<reason>.details_schema`); never a secret.

message.description: Core-written English; never parsed, never plugin text.

reason.description: A member of `components.x-busbar-reasons`; null only for `internal`.

ExactAdjustReq.description: Exact-Count adjustment profile selected only by one valid Idempotency-Key header. Key and exact body bytes identify one durable action. Runtime validates count range/scale, entry/epoch, key, pool and nonnegative resulting counts. Without the header only the legacy signed-integer request applies.

card_epoch_ms.description:
The corrected unit's card epoch: its arrival instant, unix milliseconds. The correction
lands in the budget windows, the card entry and the metering day holding it, never in those
current when it is made, and `entry` must be the entry in force at it.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

additionalProperties.description: Signed exact Count decimal. New clients send decimal strings. Legacy numeric tokens are accepted losslessly; value must fit signed i128 scale 6. Decimal exponent syntax follows Count::parse; no binary64 rounding.

entry.description: The rate-card history entry key the counts were priced with, as 40 hexadecimal digits.

key.description: The key whose counts are corrected.

lane.description: The lane (model) the counts were earned on.

pool.description:
The pool the corrected unit was dispatched through. Required, and it must name a pool this
node has configured: a pool-scoped group budget for that pool takes the correction as well
as the group-wide budgets do.

reason.description: Nonblank UTF-8 reason, at most 4096 bytes; only its hash is retained in the safe action receipt.

FlushCacheReq.description:
The `POST /api/v1/admin/auth/cache/flush` body. An absent body (or an absent `module`) flushes
every partition. Deliberately NOT `deny_unknown_fields`: the endpoint has always ignored extra
members, and tightening that would reject a call that works today.

module.description: The auth module whose cache partition to flush. Omitted = flush all.

budget_remaining_cents.description: Cents left under `budget_cap` (floored at 0); absent when no budget cap is set.

pool.description: The pool scope for a pool-qualified bucket; absent for a group-wide bucket.

requests.description: Requests admitted this window (the requests-limit truth: failures are not refunded).

GroupUsageView.description:
`GET /groups/{name}/usage`: one group's DERIVED current-window usage, one row per
enforcement bucket (each `(window, pool?)` its limits materialise), against that bucket's
caps. The dashboard read: spend/tokens/requests per tier vs the budgets, straight off the
ledger x the CURRENT rate card (reprice-on-read, nothing stored). The customer's self-service
tool consumes this per group (`user:<sub>` leaf = one person's view) and re-scopes it.

as_of.description: Epoch seconds the read was taken at (the windows below are current AS OF this instant).

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

buckets.description:
One row per enforcement bucket, in the group's resolved bucket order. Empty for a group
with only a `concurrent` limit (or none); there is no windowed ledger to read.

enabled.description: `false` = the group is FROZEN (`enabled: false`): every request through it rejects.

group.description: The group name (echoed from the path).

GroupView.description:
A group definition in the registry read (`GET /api/v1/admin/groups`,
`GET /api/v1/admin/groups/{name}`): the limit-tree read surface. Projects the `groups:` config
entry faithfully (parent chain, enabled freeze flag, the ordered limits, the `child_default`
budget template for auto-provisioned children), never a secret. This is the READ shape; the
WRITE verbs accept a `GroupCfg` verbatim (paste a config.yaml group block). Additive-only.

child_default.description:
The limit template stamped onto children auto-provisioned under this group (e.g. a
`user:<sub>` leaf on first self-mint). Skipped from the body when the group sets none.

enabled.description: `false` FREEZES the group (every request charging through it is rejected; history kept).

limits.description: The group's own limits, enforced together (AND). Order preserved from config.

parent.description:
The parent group whose limits this one is ANDed under (the enforcement chain). `None` = a
root group. Skipped from the body when absent.

Hash.description: A 32-byte digest as 64 lower-case hex characters.

HookAttachment.description:
One place a hook is attached (ADMIN-API-1.6 §8). `target` is `pools` (every pool),
`pools.<pool>`, `<section>` (a plane section's own list) or `<section>.<instance>` (one plane
instance's list); the same string is the `{target}` of `PUT|DELETE /hooks/{name}/attachments/{target}`.

instance.description: The plane instance, for `<section>.<instance>`; null for `pools` and `pools.<pool>`.

position.description: Zero-based place in the target's list; the list is the firing order.

HookDesiredStatus.description:
The DESIRED settings side of `hooks/{name}/status`: busbar's registry copy of the hook's settings
(KEY NAMES only, see [`super::HookView::settings_keys`]) and their version.

settings_keys.description: Sorted KEY NAMES of the desired settings bag, never its values.

HookHealthView.description:
The live health of one hook's transport (`GET /api/v1/admin/hooks/{name}/health`). Checks
whether the hook resolves to a LOADED `kind: hook` plugin in the process's plugin registry;
this is a plugin-LOAD status check, not a network reachability probe: it never opens a
connection, and it cannot tell you whether a `kind: hook` plugin's own configured external
endpoint (e.g. `busbar-webrequest-hook`'s `settings.url`) is actually reachable, only that the
plugin itself is loaded. Never fires the hook. Additive-only.

detail.description:
A short human note on the resolution (why `false`, or the resolved plugin's kind). Never a
secret.

reachable.description:
`Some(true)` = resolves to a loaded `kind: hook` plugin; `Some(false)` = it does not
(wrong kind, or not installed/loaded), always `Some`, never `None`, as of 1.5.0's
in-process plugin model.

HookPosition.description: Where in the target's list: the word `last`, or a zero-based place.

HookPositionWord.description: The one word a position may be.

HookReportedStatus.description:
The REPORTED settings side of `hooks/{name}/status`: what the hook says it is actually running
(present only when the hook answered `status`).

KEY NAMES only, and for a sharper reason than the desired side: the reported bag is the hook's
ECHO of the SECRET-RESOLVED settings busbar pushed it, i.e. the PLAINTEXT of every `SecretRef`,
and this read is reachable at READ-ONLY admin scope. `null` when the hook answered `status` but
reported no settings.

settings_keys.description: Sorted KEY NAMES of the observed settings bag, never its values.

HookSchemaView.description:
`GET /hooks/{name}/schema`: the hook's self-described settings JSON Schema (proxied over the
`describe` wire message), or `null` when the hook/transport does not answer.

schema.description: The hook's settings JSON Schema verbatim (an arbitrary JSON object), or `null`.

HookStatusView.description:
`GET /hooks/{name}/status`, the hook's OBSERVED state: desired vs reported settings with a
`drift` verdict, plus the hook's self-reported metrics. `reported`/`drift` are `null` and `note`
is present when the hook did not answer (fail-open); `metrics` is invariantly an array.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

drift_keys.description:
The DESIRED settings KEY NAMES the hook is not actually running: the actionable half of
`drift`, carrying names this body already serves and no value from either bag. Invariantly an
array (empty on the no-answer branch, where no drift is known).

metrics.description:
Validated + bounded self-reported metrics; each entry carries `{name, type, value}` and, when
the hook sent them, optional `labels`/`quantiles`/`estimated`/`ci_low`/`ci_high`/`help`/
`label`/`unit`/`viz`/`max` members.

schemars' blanket `JsonSchema` impl for
`serde_json::Value` renders as the JSON-Schema-2020-12 boolean `true` (`schemars-1.2.1`'s
`json_schema_impls/serdejson.rs`), which is legal 2020-12 but, nested here as this array's
`items`, is a boolean SUB-schema, and `kin-openapi` (the parser under `oapi-codegen`, which
every published SDK generates through) cannot represent one at all: the parse aborts, taking
out Python/TS/Go SDK regeneration simultaneously. `#[schemars(schema_with)]` overrides just
this field's schema to `{"type": "array", "items": {}}`; `{}` is the equivalent "accepts
anything" schema every generator DOES understand, and is what busbar-ui's own
`openapi-prep.py` already rewrites `items: true` into client-side. This is the only
`items: true` in the document; every other `additionalProperties: true` schemars emits
elsewhere is a boolean in a position `kin-openapi` handles fine and is deliberately untouched.

note.description: A short human note present only on the fail-open (no-answer) branch.

source.description: Always `"live"` (the read is a live transport query).

HookTransportView.description:
The transport half of a `HookView`. As of 1.5.0 a hook is EITHER a compiled-in kind (no
transport at all) or a signed `kind: hook` dlopen'd plugin (`target` = the plugin NAME, not a
socket path or URL); the retired 1.4.x socket/webhook sidecar transports are gone.

kind.description:
`"plugin"` for a signed dlopen'd hook plugin, or `"none"` for a hook with no plugin
transport (compiled-in kinds, or a misconfigured entry).

target.description: The plugin's NAME (not a path or URL). `None` when `kind` is `"none"`.

HookView.description:
A hook definition in the registry read (`GET /api/v1/admin/hooks`, `GET /api/v1/admin/hooks/{name}`): the
plugin catalog read. Projects the DEFINITION (kind, transport, grants, ordering, stage), never a
secret, INCLUDING the `settings:` bag, which is projected as KEY NAMES only (see
[`HookView::settings_keys`]). `global` reports whether the hook fires on EVERY request. There is
no `global_hooks:` config key to write: 1.5.3 deleted it, and a hook is now DEFINED once in the
top-level `hooks:` named map (its `module:` naming the `kind: hook` plugin that backs it) and
ATTACHED by bare name, at the reserved all-pools key `pools.hooks:`, which is what makes it
global, or at one pool's own `hooks:` list. On THIS API the same hook is written with
`global: true`; the wire and the config file are deliberately different surfaces. Live connection
status (`health`) is a separate endpoint. Additive-only.

`groups:` and `phase:` are the config-file SELECTION axes (which callers, which pipeline stages),
and this view used to omit both. That was not a decision to keep them file-only: both are
WRITABLE over this API (`POST`/`PUT /hooks` deserialize `config::HookCfg` verbatim, which is the
documented "paste a `hooks:` entry" contract), so omitting them made a field an operator can set
through the API one they could not read back through it. `groups` and the stage pair
(`phase` + `fires_at`) close that.

attachments.description:
Hook attach points (§8): every list this hook is attached to, with its place in the list.
`instance` is the plane instance for a plane-section attach point, else null.

default.description: Whether this hook replaces the default ordering hook for pools with no named base.

fires_at.description: The effective stage set in pipeline order, computed by the runtime firing predicate.

global.description: Whether this hook fires on every request (globally wired).

groups.description:
The `groups:` CALLER SCOPE exactly as configured: the caller groups this hook fires for,
empty meaning ALL callers (unscoped). The other half of "when does this hook run", and the
same writable-but-unreadable gap `phase` had.

on_empty.description:
Configured empty-intersection fallback: `"weighted"` | `"reject"` | `"first"`.
`null` preserves an omitted override, whose runtime default is fail-closed.

on_error.description:
Gate fallback on timeout/error, a CLOSED, unambiguous string union: one of the
reserved terminals (`"weighted"` | `"reject"` | `"first"` | `"nothing"`) or the NAME of the
fallback hook the chain continues through. Unambiguous by construction: the terminal words
are ILLEGAL hook names on every write path (`config::RESERVED_HOOK_NAMES`), so a value in
the terminal set is always a terminal and anything else is always a hook reference.

phase.description: The canonical configured stage list. Empty selects the fixed core stages.

priority.description: Rewrite/reject ordering key (transform-chain order + reject tie-break).

settings_keys.description:
The KEY NAMES of the hook's opaque settings bag, sorted, WITHOUT their values, the same
redacted projection [`NamedDefView::settings_keys`] carries, produced by the same helper.

This used to be the bag itself, under a doc comment claiming hook settings are "never a
secret by contract". That claim was retracted for `NamedDefView` and it is no more true here:
a hook's settings bag is a `SecretRef` carrier by design (resolved before the native hook opens),
and `config::secret::resolve_settings` forwards a
non-object bag verbatim, so a literal credential is fully supported too. `GET /hooks` and
`GET /hooks/{name}` serve this at READ-ONLY admin scope. The values are readable only where
they are writable: the config file and the config overlay.

signals.description: Requested signal catalog names, in configured order.

InfoCrypto.description:
`InfoView.crypto` (ADMIN-API-1.6-ONE-MODEL §10.1, E-17): the one validated-mode answer, the same
values `core/process` `state.crypto` serves.

validated_mode.description:
True only when the linked crypto backend states a validation; derived from that statement
alone, never from the backend's name, a feature, an entitlement or configuration.

validation.description: The linked backend's validation statement (a certificate reference), or null.

InfoView.description:
`GET /api/v1/admin/info`: this node's identity and nothing else (ADMIN-API-1.6-ONE-MODEL §10.1).
Every admin credential reads it, so it names no topology, no compiled-in plugin and no
process-local counter: node lease rows are the `core/process` view `nodes`, counts come from
`/kinds`, and the `/kinds` ETag is the discovery revision.

config_generation.description:
The durable config generation (ADMIN-API-1.6 6.1): advanced in the Store before every
publication, so it never repeats across restarts. The ETag of every config resource is
`"<deployment_id>.<config_generation>"`.

x-busbar-exact-number.client: lossless-number-token-v1; preserve raw token before binary64 conversion

crypto.description:
Whether this binary runs a validated crypto module, and the linked backend's validation
statement (E-17). The backend's name and module version are `core/process` `state.crypto`.

deployment_id.description:
This deployment's identity (`dep_` + 32 hex, opaque): kept once in the Store, the same
for every node and every restart. Absent only before the process has booted its Store.

incarnation.description:
This process's incarnation, the join-id term (`{node_id}.{incarnation}.{unit_key}`): a
random 128-bit process generation, shared with the `/metrics` build_info series. Stable

UpdateKeyReq.description:
Partial update to an existing key. Keys are PURE AUTH (1.5.0), so the mutable surface is
auth-shaped only. Every field is optional; only the present ones change. The credential, name,
allowed-pools, and labels are immutable here (rotate/recreate for those).

`group` is THREE-STATE via serde double-option (`Option<Option<String>>`):
- absent (`#[serde(default)]` -> outer `None`): leave the binding unchanged.
- JSON `null` (`Some(None)`): UNBIND to no group (authed + unlimited).
- a value (`Some(Some(name))`): REBIND to that group (must exist; mint-parity check).

A single `Option<T>` could not tell absent from present-null, so a binding could never be
cleared once set. `enabled` is a plain `Option<bool>` (a bool has no clear state). The 1.4.x
cap fields (`rpm_limit`/`tpm_limit`/`max_budget_cents`) are GONE: limits live on the group.

group.description: Omitted preserves binding; null explicitly unbinds; a string rebinds to an existing group.

post.description: Correct counts at the original card epoch. With Idempotency-Key, the durable exact-Count profile binds actor/action to exact bytes and returns AdjustmentActionView. Without it, retain legacy signed-integer/nonretryable semantics. Applied, not_applied and unknown are distinct outcomes; never infer no effect from a failed response.

parameters.description: Selects durable exact-Count action profile. Exactly one ASCII graphic value (1..128 bytes). Authenticated actor + adjust + header identify a stable action; SHA256 binds exact body bytes. Receipts/claims do not automatically expire or recycle and survive restart. Identical retries return the retained outcome; changed bytes conflict. Without this header the legacy route is not safe to blindly retry.

post.description: The body names the release; one this node does not run is refused and seals nothing. The committed release is sealed on the node journal before the answer names its position and chain hash. Honors an `Idempotency-Key` header (per-principal, ~10min replay): a retry with the same key and body answers the first commit and seals nothing again.

parameters.description: Optional replay action identity scoped to authenticated actor, operation and target. Retained about 10 minutes. Exact request bytes must match. Credential secret replay is process-local; a durable applied receipt survives restart without retaining the secret. See operation recovery semantics before retrying.

parameters.description: The current config-generation ETag. New instance_edit dispatch requires exactly one strong ETag even when global require_if_match is false; missing is 428, weak/wildcard/malformed is 400, stale is 409. Exact authenticated idempotent replay returns its retained outcome without a new effect. Other request modes retain their existing conditional-write policy.
parameters.name: If-Match

parameters.description: Required exactly once for instance_edit; optional for other settings request modes. Use 1..128 ASCII letters, digits, dot, underscore, colon or hyphen. The authenticated principal and key retain the exact separately framed method, path, query and body identity. Identical authenticated replay returns the original outcome and ETag before checking the original now-stale precondition; changed request bytes conflict. A failed response or canceled HTTP request does not prove no effect. Preserve this key for operation lookup and uncertain-outcome recovery; never automatically retry under a new key.
parameters.name: Idempotency-Key

oneOf.description: Replace named root settings sections, merging omitted sections with the existing overlay. Null preserves a section. A mutable configuration stores changes through its configured Store; a locked configuration refuses changes. Listen, TLS and Store changes require restart. oneOf.title: ConfigSettingsReplacement

document_patch.description: Lowest-priority Store overlay over config.yaml, parsed with boot's schema. RFC6901 paths; strict sequence indices replace existing entries, terminal - appends. Within one request, indices name the input snapshot; sets precede descending removals. Each subsequent request addresses the current authored document. Null is a value, removal is explicit. Omitted values including secrets survive. Overlapping paths and edits shadowed by existing typed overlays are refused. Restart-only fields are reported. Patch history is bounded to 4096 total operations and 1 MiB; pointer depth is at most 128. Limit violations reject the transaction.

providers_patch.description: Edits providers.yaml through its boot grammar in the same Store transaction. Paths start with catalog entry names. Deployment overrides that shadow an edit are refused.

reset_document_paths.description: Forget only these exact prior document edits before merging the new edit; typed overlays are never removed.

reset_providers_paths.description: Forget only these exact prior catalog edits before merging providers_patch.

oneOf.description: Discovered instance settings edit on the existing config transaction. New dispatch requires one strong current config ETag in If-Match and one Idempotency-Key. Omitted settings survive; set replaces complete top-level values; null is a value; remove is explicit. Requires current image/schema/source identity. The actual authoring parser, secret policy, source binding, typed overlay precedence and runtime validation remain authoritative. Store/secret changes can require restart; persisted configuration is not physical activation. Exact method/path/query/body replay retains the original outcome; an error receipt is not proof of no effect.

get.description: `view=effective` (the default) is the resolved generation: every section the kernel reads back (plugin and plane sections included) and `process`, the command-line and environment inputs. `view=declared` is the configuration as written, by `layer`: `base` (the operator's file as it stands), `overlay` (the Store overlay's per-section documents, tombstones, document-patch paths and version) or `merged` (both side by side, the default). `section=<dotted key>` narrows the sections served. Every secret position (a secret-named field, a plugin setting the plugin did not declare public, a private key) is `{set, secret_ref}`: never a value, never a hash of one; public key material is a `sha256` fingerprint. `digest` is over the projected sections. The ETag is the config ETag.

parameters.description: `effective` (default): the resolved generation. `declared`: the configuration as written.
parameters.name: view

parameters.description: With `view=declared`: `base` (the file as written), `overlay` (the Store overlay) or `merged` (both, the default). The effective view is `merged` only.
parameters.name: layer

parameters.description: A dotted key (`limits.request_body_max_bytes`) narrowing the sections served; `404` when no layer holds it.

The instance-bound recovery facade checks current authority and confirms a durable, attributed verdict before reposting or releasing dependent negative work. An expired receipt never proves not-landed. The same verdict, version, actor and reason replays its durable outcome; a conflicting retry is refused. The Store operation survives cancellation of the HTTP waiter. No raw payload, credential or mutable dollar balance is returned.

get.summary: The plugin settings JSON Schema for every kind. source=installed_archive reads the named disk artifact, optionally fenced by expected_archive_sha256; it never substitutes a loaded generation. source=linked_statement reads a linked plane/transport declaration cached during startup. Without source, resolve the loaded module by name or alias, then the linked declaration cache. Canonical Statement first, legacy manifest field only when the Statement carries no schema. Dropped plugins are read from the signed manifest without opening the library; linked plugins publish their Statement. `hook` plugins keep the live describe-proxy behavior when describe answers (source: describe); a loaded hook whose describe answers null falls back server-side to the manifest baseline (source: manifest)

get.description: A read-time projection of this node's sealed per-unit audit records, oldest first. `next_cursor` is always a string; `complete: true` means caught up. With no cursor the feed starts at the oldest retained record. A request scans at most 10000 sealed records, so a filtered page may be short or empty with a cursor that continues. Records are per node: the `core/process` view `nodes` lists every node. Spend is priced at read by the rule `GET /usage` uses. A read: it mutates nothing and is never posture-gated.

post.description: A counterparty is approved at the catalogue hash it last reported, which clears its quarantine; an item at the digest it was last sighted at. Both members of the body are required: `expected_digest` is the digest reviewed from `GET /trust` (omitted: 428 `reviewed_digest_required`; not current: 409 `reviewed_digest_stale`, nothing changes). Approve is strict: `expected_digest` must equal the current `seen`, and `null` is valid only while the key was never sighted. The decision is kept durably before the answer and outlives a restart; every attempt is audited as `trust_approve` or `trust_revoke`, naming the key. `Idempotency-Key` (1..128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`; it is echoed as the kept decision's `operation`) makes the request replayable: the same key and bytes answer the original outcome with `idempotent-replayed: true` and never decide again; other bytes are 409 `idempotency_mismatch`, a request still running 409 `idempotency_in_flight`. A durable write whose outcome is unknown answers 503 `service_unavailable` with `details` naming the attempt: replay the same key and bytes to resolve it, to 200 when it is in force or to 409 `outcome_not_applied` when the store proves it never applied; until then it stays the same 503 (read the key's state and decide again under a new key). `x-busbar-trust-effect` classifies every answer: `applied`, `not_applied` or `unknown`.

post.summary: Approve one trust key at the digest the operator reviewed

post.description: Refused until approved again: a counterparty revoked refuses everything at it, an item revoked refuses it over its configured approval. Both members of the body are required: `expected_digest` is the digest reviewed from `GET /trust` (omitted: 428 `reviewed_digest_required`; not current: 409 `reviewed_digest_stale`, nothing changes). Revoke accepts the current `seen` or the current `approved` digest; `null` matches a null one of them. The decision is kept durably before the answer and outlives a restart; every attempt is audited as `trust_approve` or `trust_revoke`, naming the key. `Idempotency-Key` (1..128 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 . _ : -`; it is echoed as the kept decision's `operation`) makes the request replayable: the same key and bytes answer the original outcome with `idempotent-replayed: true` and never decide again; other bytes are 409 `idempotency_mismatch`, a request still running 409 `idempotency_in_flight`. A durable write whose outcome is unknown answers 503 `service_unavailable` with `details` naming the attempt: replay the same key and bytes to resolve it, to 200 when it is in force or to 409 `outcome_not_applied` when the store proves it never applied; until then it stays the same 503 (read the key's state and decide again under a new key). `x-busbar-trust-effect` classifies every answer: `applied`, `not_applied` or `unknown`.

request_timing.aggregation: offsets overlap; never sum them as disjoint durations; busy_ns/idle_ns are span entry accounting, not CPU profiling
request_timing.clock: monotonic elapsed microseconds from the attempt timing guard after member selection; route_wait_us is the preceding member selection duration
request_timing.coverage: selected request-pump attempts, including normal, degraded and retry attempts; not pre-route refusals or session traffic outside the request pump
request_timing.identity: trace_id/parent_span_id link the request; the request_attempts parent span scopes attempt ordinals, including separate session turns; retry_of_attempt names its predecessor

intervals.attempt_end_us: pump attempt terminated, retried, or was abandoned
intervals.cancelled_us: pump observed cancellation; cancel_reason is the engine reason code
intervals.far_end_last_us: far-end terminal piece or end-of-pieces without cut/failover
intervals.first_body_us: first nonempty non-trailer far-end bytes; not a token event or TTFT
intervals.producer_complete_us: pump completed its output writes; not proof of remote client consumption
intervals.response_ready_us: first observed far-end status or nonempty bytes; not stream completion
intervals.route_wait_us: member selection, including waits within selection; not an isolated queue duration

request_timing.loss: bounded best-effort exporter admission and queue; host refusals call exporter shed; inspect exporter status for loss, absence is not zero loss or complete coverage
request_timing.metrics: existing producer_drive and response_ready cumulative distributions are unchanged
request_timing.privacy: added timing fields contain generated identity, destination index, fixed outcomes and timings only; no body, headers, prompt, credential or provider error text; other span attributes retain the existing exporter policy
request_timing.requires: enabled hot-path tracing and an exporter taking full span records
request_timing.sampling: no producer probabilistic sampling; disabled/level-filtered tracing omits records; exporter sampling is exporter-specific

PluginFetch.description:
One `plugins.fetch:` entry — an UNTAGGED enum discriminated by which key is present. `github` is a
`org/repo@tag` release ref (asset resolved by the loader); `url` is a direct tarball URL; `env`
names an environment variable holding a URL (or `url@sha256`). `sha256` (github/url) is the
lowercase-hex integrity pin: it is BOTH the download-skip cache key (a file in `dir` already
hashing to it ⇒ no network) and the verify-before-write gate. Per-variant `deny_unknown_fields`
so a typo'd key can't be silently reinterpreted as a different variant.

PluginPublisher.description: One operator-authorized publisher and its exact plugin names and overlapping keys.

PluginPublisherKey.description: A configured Ed25519 publisher key. Revoked keys remain visible but never admit code.

Plugins.description:
The top-level `plugins:` block — the ONLY configuration surface of the dynamic plugin subsystem.
A plugin is a plugin: store, auth, and hook plugins share this one block (one directory, one
trust model, one master switch); the manifest `kind` inside each signed tarball selects which
engine subsystem consumes it.

dir.description:
Directory the signed plugin tarballs live in. Default `plugins` (relative to the working
directory).

enabled.description:
MASTER SWITCH, default FALSE. When false (or the whole `plugins:` block is absent), NO
plugin is ever loaded — a tarball dropped into the directory is INERT. Referencing a plugin
while disabled (`store.module:` other than `memory`) is a BOOT ERROR naming this flag.

fetch.description:
Declarative plugin FETCH list (`plugins.fetch:`): tarballs busbar downloads into `dir` at
boot (fatal-on-miss) and on `POST /plugins/reload` (warn-on-miss) BEFORE preflight. Each entry
is a github release ref, a direct url, or an env var holding one — optionally sha256-pinned
(integrity + download-skip cache key). NOT consulted by `--validate` (zero-network contract).
Signature verification remains the trust gate; sha256 is integrity/cache only. Default empty.

min_versions.description:
ANTI-DOWNGRADE floors: plugin canonical `name` -> minimum acceptable `version`. Applies to
first- and third-party alike, and is SEPARATE from the automatic first-party floor (the
per-name high-water mark the registry build maintains, which needs no
configuration). A floored plugin must prove (trusted signature, version at/above the floor)
that it meets the floor; nothing else loads it. Sibling of `trust` (a version axis, not a
trust axis).

trust.description:
Trust policy for plugin signatures. busbar's OWN release key is EMBEDDED in the binary —
first-party plugins verify with zero configuration; this block is for THIRD-PARTY keys and
the explicit untrusted opt-ins.
